building.top_level_shape: Electron desktop app ("Munder Difflin harness / Camelot Trihamlet") using electron-vite, node-pty for real Claude Code / agent CLI PTYs, React 18 + Zustand renderer, and PixiJS for the walking-avatar office scene. Two coexisting renderer shells wired at build time (`main.tsx` picks between them): the LEGACY `App.tsx` (full-screen PixiJS floor + right-side agent detail panel) and the NEW `CrewShell.tsx` (lazygit-shaped 3-pane building view with a floor-stack of Tiny-Tower tiles, a conversation-centerpiece, a detail pane, and the raw-traces drawer). Ships as a native Electron package (`out/main/index.js` + `out/preload/index.js` + a `pick-office.ps1` / `run-office.ps1` launcher pair) with an embedded `copilot-pwa/` service-worker PWA that a phone can hit for the remote-control / god-reply thread. On-disk state lives under a per-office `hive/` git repo (single-committer: main process only; agents just drop files).

key_atoms.name: GOD orchestrator
key_atoms.purpose: The god-agent bootstrap + orchestrator glue. Spawns the god PTY (id='god', name='Parthy'/per-floor override) into the harnessHome cwd, runs the /remote-control + INITIAL_GOD_PROMPT boot sequence gated by the TUI-readiness bootGate, drives hive.ts, wires all worker hook events (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PreCompact/Stop/Notification/UserPromptSubmit/PreInvocation/PostInvocation) to floor state, handles idle-inbox nudging with per-agent NUDGE_COOLDOWN_MS + `nudged`-ref dedup, and enforces the breaker precedence pin. Hive.ts on the main side (src/main/hive.ts, 1588 lines) is the on-disk router that this hook drives — registry.json, tasks.json, per-agent inbox/outbox/memory.md/cursor.json, log.jsonl, board.md, PROTOCOL.md, single-committer git.

key_atoms.name: Worker tile / AgentStrip
key_atoms.purpose: Bottom strip of live-agent tiles in the classic App shell — each tile is one PTY, shows portrait/name/status/action, click to select. AgentCard.tsx + AgentControlStrip.tsx render richer per-agent controls. AgentDetailPanel.tsx is the right-side deep view for one worker (terminal + command bar + queue).

key_atoms.name: Walking-avatar scene (OfficeFloor)
key_atoms.purpose: 1895-line PixiJS scene: Tiled map (office.tmj), tileset atlas, Camera, Character sprites with cast portraits, pathfinding, station stations (desk/shelf/terminal/board/mailbox/web/mcp), coffee economy, cafeteria breaks, idle errands (water plants/cig break/etc), gossip-vs-suckup lines when Michael walks by, MessageEnvelope handoff-flying, and the ThoughtBubble/ToolBubble pop-ups. THIS is 'agents-as-interface' — the load-bearing metaphor of the whole product.

key_atoms.name: Spawn-a-real-Claude mechanism
key_atoms.purpose: The single spawn path used by both the AddAgentModal (human click) and the god's spawn-request poller (organ-driven). Mints ptyId=`pty-<agentId>`, calls `window.cth.spawnPty` with a hive AgentMeta, closes the bootGate, and pushes an Agent record with status='idle', action='starting up'. The PTY IS a real live `claude` process — no simulation. Main-side spawn: src/main/pty.ts + hive.ts.ensureAgent injects hive-aware env + args (--add-dir hive root, hooks pointing at cth-hook.cjs).

key_atoms.name: Streamed-output terminal
key_atoms.purpose: Persistent xterm.js pool: one xterm+WebGL renderer per ptyId, pre-warmed at spawn, attaches to the DOM on demand — the 'live claude output stream' the empty-floor CTA promises. PtyTerminalView.tsx, FullscreenTerminal.tsx and crew/GodTerminalLens.tsx all mount from the same pool, so the buffer is warm the moment a tile is clicked.

key_atoms.name: God terminal lens
key_atoms.purpose: The crew shell's centerpiece view of the god's live TUI — READ-ONLY by default (xterm disableStdin), 'unlock typing' toggle for deliberate write-through, One-Half-Dark theme, JetBrainsMono NF font. Supports REMOTE floors via `remotePtyList` + the loopback PTY gateway (remoteTranscript.ts). This is the 'fully interrupting me → but not' resolution of Carlos's complaint.

key_atoms.name: Thought-line / status-line rendering
key_atoms.purpose: The pinned cloud above each avatar's head. Reads `agent.action` (`using Read`, `compacting context`, `reading inbox`, `running the floor`, `thinking`, or the first 6 words of `lastPrompt`) — empty text renders an animated '…' (thinking dots). Fade-in/linger/fade-out state machine, camera-zoom counter-scaling, world-bounds clamping so a corner avatar's cloud never leaves the map. Sibling ToolBubble.ts is the darker speech bubble for tool-glyph mutters.

key_atoms.name: Liveness/floor-state oracle
key_atoms.purpose: Lines 1140–1360-ish: the 'unfuckable' floor-state protocol. Main writes claim.json (BOOT_NONCE + pid + boot-time, atomic, once at boot — Tier A + Tier B named-mutex holder via child PowerShell) and beat.json (monotonic seq, ~10s cadence, only written while the RENDERER keeps beating via `hive:beat` IPC — a wedged renderer with live main reads STALE, never false-green). The reader is `.claude/tools/floor-state.cjs` (external) which emits verdict enum: alive / wedged / dead / down / never-booted / unverified / stale-unknown / probably-alive / unknown. Verdict is overlaid onto pulse.json.oracleState so left-pane FloorStack tiles and centerpiece PulsePanel show ONE truth.

key_atoms.name: Awareness beat (renderer half)
key_atoms.purpose: React error-boundary that also fires `window.cth.beat()` on interval; if the cockpit render throws, the beat stops, main stops touching beat.json, and the oracle reads WEDGED. This is the 'the boundary IS the honesty spine' pattern — a rendering failure MUST degrade to a red verdict, never a stuck green.

key_atoms.name: Fan-out visualization: message envelopes
key_atoms.purpose: Every hive-routed message flies as a paper-envelope sprite from sender desk to recipient desk (or to the office door for 'human' recipients — escalations). Main-process router emits `onHiveMessage({from, targets[], act, needsHuman})`; the scene spawns one envelope per target. This IS the god→worker fan-out visualization — no explicit tree/graph edges, just physical paper crossing the office.

key_atoms.name: Floor stack (crew shell)
key_atoms.purpose: Tiny-Tower vertical stack of floor TILES in the crew shell's LEFT pane. One tile per floor (penthouse/spine/atlas/hestia/crew), each showing god name, worker roster, oracle-verdict dot+word (OV_META), recent activity, and card counts (todo/doing/blocked/done). Reads the building feed (buildingFeed.ts). All floors concurrent — hidden scenes stay mounted with ticker stopped.

key_atoms.name: Needs-you strip
key_atoms.purpose: HITL queue. Aggregates blocked agents (status='blocked' or blockReason set) + unanswered task humanQA entries. Renders nothing when empty (zero chrome). Read-only surface — the answer flow lives elsewhere (composer / task detail / god's own session). Same posture as cockpit-v2's NEEDS-YOU plane.

key_atoms.name: Pulse panel + PulseView

Reads `.offices/main/hive/pulse.json` written by a 60s derived-only distiller (pulse.cjs) — heartbeat age, blockedOnHuman ranked, shipped, burning, per-floor oracleState, narrative line. STALE_MS=3min → distiller-not-running is honestly reported, never frozen-fresh. Strip variant sits above the conversation; PulseView is a top-level view.

key_atoms.name: Command Center

key_atoms.name: Copilot PWA (phone surface)

key_atoms.name: Closing time protocol
key_atoms.purpose: Graceful shutdown: mails god a shutdown brief, god broadcasts to team, each worker commits/parks WIP + appends state to memory.md + ACKs, god sends CLOSING-TIME-COMPLETE, main tears down. Never types into terminals — pure hive-mail rails. This is a LIFECYCLE HOOK Happy could steal as-is.

In feed-cast mode, remote-floor scenes render from the building feed instead of the local store — same scene, different data.

ia_patterns.name: Everything-is-a-hive-file
ia_patterns.description: IA truth is on disk under `<harnessHome>/hive/`: registry.json (agents), tasks.json (kanban), board.md (shared blackboard), log.jsonl (append-only), per-agent {identity.md, memory.md, inbox/, outbox/, cursor.json, .gitignore}. UI is a view onto files; the god is the SOLE scribe of board.md. Consistent with the work-first-cockpit-spec §2 'files = self' invariant.

building.data_flow: Truth on disk under `<harnessHome>/hive/` (registry.json, tasks.json, board.md, per-agent inbox/outbox/memory.md, log.jsonl, plus per-host claim.json + beat.json + fleet.json). Push-side wire is Claude Code HOOKS: every agent's shim (`hive/bin/cth-hook.cjs`, written at bootstrap) opens a UDS/named-pipe (hive/hooks.sock on POSIX, `\\.\pipe\munder-difflin-<hash>` on Windows) to the main process and forwards PreToolUse / PostToolUse / PreCompact / PostCompact / UserPromptSubmit / Notification / Stop / SubagentStop / SessionStart / PreInvocation / PostInvocation events, plus the statusline shim forwards exact context tokens+limit after every response. Main forwards via `hive:hookEvent` IPC; useHive.ts effect #2 is the giant switch that maps every event to `updateAgent({status, action, currentStation, carrying, contextTokens, contextLimit})`. Additional streams: `onHiveMessage` (routed hive mail — drives envelope sprites), `onBreakerState` (circuit-breaker level with PRECEDENCE over hook state — pins 'looping' until Stop), `onHiveTerminalHandoff` (non-Claude providers get hive mail as PTY-typed work orders), `onHiveContextUpdate` (statusline exact context), plus fs.watch on god/inbox for spawn-requests. Backfill loops: 15s poll of agentContext (transcript-derived tokens for agents whose statusline hasn't fired), 7s poll of hive:tasks for the NeedsYouStrip humanQA count, 8s poll of the building feed (buildingFeed.ts) for cross-floor tiles, 15s poll of pulse.json. Router polling: main-side hive.ts drains each agent's outbox into recipients' inboxes on interval (single-committer git per drain). The renderer NEVER polls the god's PTY buffer — output flows via the persistent xterm inside terminalPool, subscribed to the raw PTY stream at spawn.

walking_avatar_scene.tech: PixiJS v8 (with `pixi.js/unsafe-eval` shim for Electron CSP), Tiled JSON maps (office.tmj imported as raw text and parsed), three tilesets (office-tileset.png embedded + a5-office-floors-walls.png + interiors.png), custom TiledMapRenderer.ts, Camera.ts, Character.ts sprites with 4-facing animation frames from cast.ts (portraitArt.ts for the tile portraits), pathfinding.ts for A* on the collision grid, DeskScreen.ts for the desk-monitor overlay lit while seated, ThoughtBubble.ts + ToolBubble.ts for the pop-ups, MessageEnvelope.ts for flying mail. 1895 lines total.
walking_avatar_scene.description: Full-floor Tiled office map — CEO office (Michael/god's private room, top-left corner), 6 pc- open-plan desks, named function-role desks (chief-architect / product-manager / team-lead / backend-engineer / ui-ux-expert / data-engineer / project-manager / market-researcher / agent-organizer), conference room overflow, break room (coffee machine + sink + mug tray + snack vending + fridge + water dispenser + plants + open smoking window). Each Agent maps to a Character sprite: canonical `castForAgent(agent)` picks the face (matching the portrait), a SeatPool assigns desks in PRIMARY_SEAT_NAMES order (first agent → desk-ceo, then pc-1..6, then named roles). Sprites walk to stations driven by TOOL_STATION mapping (Read→shelf, Edit/Write→desk, Bash→terminal, WebFetch/Search→web, TodoWrite→board, Task→mailbox, mcp__*→mcp). Idle behavior: cafeteria breaks with two-actor scripted dialogues (cafeteriaLines.ts pickExchange), errands (water plants, letting-air-in at window, hydration break, fridge peek, shelf browse, scrap-paper bin), Michael's boss-only smoke break at the window, gossip-vs-suckup line switch when Michael walks past a worker. Task-board pin/take/archive movements: a sprite physically pins a sticky-note, walks to grab its assignment, files it as done. Envelopes fly desk-to-desk on every routed hive message (or to the door for human escalations). Feed-cast mode renders REMOTE floors' scenes from the building feed (host-hive surfaces go inert). The scene is CLICK-OPERABLE — a character click routes to `onAgentSelect(agentId)`, hover emits `onAgentHover(info)` for a CK-style tooltip card.

building.god_worker_fan_out_pattern: Fan-out is PHYSICAL PAPER, not a tree/graph. Main-process hive router emits `onHiveMessage({from, targets[], act, needsHuman})` for every routed hive mail. `OfficeFloor.tsx` calls `spawnHandoff(from, target, act, needsHuman)` for each target — a MessageEnvelope sprite spawns at the sender's desk pixel position and flies (a clean parabolic arc, endpoints snapshotted at spawn so mid-flight avatar drift doesn't distort the path) to the recipient desk (or to the office entrance door for `to='human'` escalations). MAX_ENVELOPES cap prevents scene overload. `act` (`request/inform/propose/query/agree/refuse/done`) tints the envelope; `needsHuman` marks it. Additional fan-out cues: the god's PreToolUse events firing `Task` route to the mailbox station (a sub-agent handoff LOOKS like the god walking to the outbox); when a broadcast lands, the router emits one event with N targets and N envelopes fly at once. There is NO drawn tree, NO graph edges, NO nested tiles — the metaphor IS the visualization. Complementary crew-shell surface: DispatchLedger (dispatchLedger.ts) records opDispatch entries and PulsePanel's intent rail counts pending intents.
building.liveness_oracle_pattern: Two-layer floor-state oracle, exact match to the parthenogenesis floor-state design (docs referenced: `parthenogenesis/docs/building-awareness-final-form-2026-06-15.md`). LAYER 1 (claim): main writes `<hive>/claim.json` ONCE at boot with `{ pid, bootNonce=random 8-byte hex, bootAt=Date.now(), ownProcessStartMs (shell-out to Get-Process, one-shot), instanceId }` — Tier A stand-in for the OS lock; oracle asks the KERNEL `process.kill(pid,0)` + start-time EQUALITY cross-check (defeats PID reuse — no tolerance window). Tier B upgrade: a child PowerShell process holds an open handle on a named kernel mutex `Global\\parthy-floor-<id>-<nonce>`; the kernel annihilates it on death/reboot/power-loss so no stale claim is possible. holderRespawnTimes sliding-window budget (10 respawns per 5 min) prevents crash-loop, but exhaustion is safe — degrades to Tier A. LAYER 2 (beat): `<hive>/beat.json` written atomically (tmp+fsync+rename in the SAME dir → EXDEV-safe) with a MONOTONIC `beatSeq` every BEAT_INTERVAL_MS=10s — BUT ONLY WHILE the RENDERER has called `hive:beat` within the last BEAT_FRESH_MS=20s. A wedged/crashed renderer with live main → beat.json ages → reads STALE, never false green. The renderer's `AwarenessBeat.tsx` React error-boundary fires the beat and STOPS on render-death so the honesty-spine failure mode is 'red', never 'stuck green'. Oracle verdicts (rendered by both FloorStack tile and PulsePanel tile from ONE source pulse.json.oracleState): alive / wedged / dead / down / never-booted / unverified / stale-unknown / probably-alive / unknown — each with dedicated color + word. Both claim.json + beat.json are per-HOST runtime state and gitignored (hive.ts line 285).
building.spawn_claude_output_stream_mechanism: Path from click to visible stream: (1) User clicks 'add agent' in AddAgentModal or empty-floor CTA, or god's spawn-request organ drops a JSON into `<hive>/agents/god/inbox/spawn-requests/`. (2) `spawnHiveAgent(input)` in `store/spawnAgent.ts` mints `ptyId='pty-<agentId>'`, tokenizes the command, calls `markAgentSpawned(id)` to close the bootGate, then invokes `window.cth.spawnPty({...})`. (3) Main-side `pty.ts` uses node-pty to fork a real `claude` process (Windows-wrapped via cmd.exe /c when the target isn't a .exe — WinGet claude.exe launches directly), with hive.ts.ensureAgent-injected env (HIVE_ROOT, HIVE_AGENT_ID, HIVE_HOOKS_SOCK, OTEL endpoint if set) and args (--permission-mode bypassPermissions, --add-dir on hive root, hooks config pointing at `hive/bin/cth-hook.cjs`). (4) Main opens `onPtyData` and multicasts each chunk to any subscribing renderer via IPC AND to the persistent xterm entry in `terminalPool.ts`, which subscribes for the app's lifetime — so the buffer is warm and scrollable from the FIRST byte even if no view is currently mounted. (5) The renderer's Agent record gets `ptyId` set; `useEffect` in App.tsx calls `acquireTerminal(ptyId)` at once — pre-warming the xterm. (6) When the user clicks the agent tile, `AgentDetailPanel` (classic) or `GodTerminalLens` (crew) `attachTerminal(entry, hostRef.current)` — the WebGL xterm re-parents into the DOM instantly with full history. bootGate opens on the CLI's FIRST hook or statusline signal (SessionStart at earliest), at which point the boot placeholder action 'starting up'/'reconnecting…' flips to 'idle', the inbox-wake dedup resets, and the auto-typer hold releases. God's boot ALSO types `/remote-control` + the INITIAL_GOD_PROMPT orientation via `submitToPty` (bracketed-paste ESC[200~...ESC[201~ + separate \\r, serialized per PTY through `writeChains` so concurrent callers can't jam). A GOD_PROMPT_ACK_MS=45s watchdog re-types the orientation once if no UserPromptSubmit hook lands.

lifecycle_hooks: CLOSING TIME (src/main/closingTime.ts): human clicks 'closing time' in QuitWarningModal → main mails god shutdown brief → god broadcasts to team → each worker commits/parks WIP + appends state+next-steps to memory.md + replies with CLOSING-TIME-ACK subject → god waits for all ACKs, saves own memory, sends CLOSING-TIME-COMPLETE → main tears down. Progress streams to renderer via `onClosingTime({phase:'started'|'progress'|'complete'|'timeout'|'cancelled', acked, total})`. Rides existing hive rails only — never types into terminals.

BOOT-GATE (src/renderer/src/store/bootGate.ts): closes the auto-typer gate at `markAgentSpawned(id)` BEFORE the PTY exists; opens on the CLI's REAL first hook OR statusline signal via `markAgentTuiReady(id)`, resets inbox-wake dedup, flips 'starting up' action to 'idle'. GOD_TUI_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=10min budget with 'superseded'/'timeout' signals so a StrictMode remount or a re-spawn cleanly cancels stale waiters.

GRACE HOLD (bootGate.holdAgentGrace): a boot-hold window (BOOT_GRACE_MS = GOD_BOOT_MS 4s + REMOTE_CONTROL_SETTLE_MS 5s + 2.5s) during which the nudge/queue-drain typers are held OFF so they can't jam the boot sequence (`/remote-control` + orientation prompt).

ORIENTATION WATCHDOG (useHive armGodBoot): GOD_PROMPT_ACK_MS=45s — if `godPromptAckAt` (stamped on god's UserPromptSubmit hook) hasn't advanced past the type-time, the one-shot orientation prompt was eaten (modal/focus glitch); re-type it once.
NUDGE COOLDOWN (useHive NUDGE_COOLDOWN_MS=2s + `nudged`-ref content dedup): per-agent minimum gap + last-message-id dedup so a burst of 5 contracts fires ONE nudge, not 5.

BREAKER PRECEDENCE (useHive effect 2b + breakerLevel ref): a 'constrained'/'stopped' breaker state pins avatar to 'looping' and blocks hook-driven status flips until a genuine Stop clears it — kills the 'working-flicker' the spec calls out.

RECONCILE-WITH-LIVE-PTYS (App.tsx effect line 105): after a renderer reload (Vite HMR, laptop sleep) `window.cth.listPtys()` → `reconcileWithLivePtys` keeps restored agents whose PTY survived and drops the ones that truly died.

TERMINAL POOL PRE-WARM (App.tsx effect line 80): for every agent with a ptyId, `acquireTerminal(ptyId)` — WebGL xterm subscribes to the PTY stream even before the tile is clicked, so history is warm on first attach.

CLAIM/BEAT LIFECYCLE (main/index.ts around 1140-1360): claim.json written at boot, held by Tier B mutex-holder child; beat.json monotonic every 10s only while renderer beats; holderRespawnTimes sliding-window rebounds a killed holder; whole thing self-heals from claim demolition/kernel death/reboot.
what_the_building_does_that_happy_cannot: Physically shows an office FLOOR with walking avatars where each agent IS a sprite that moves to a work station (desk/shelf/terminal/board/mailbox/web/mcp) matching the tool it just used, mediated by real Claude Code PreToolUse hook events — Happy's cockpit-v2 shows tile status but no spatial metaphor, no motion, and no per-tool station mapping.

Streams the actual claude PTY output byte-for-byte in a persistent WebGL xterm (terminalPool) — the god's live TUI as-is, including thinking, tool calls, permission prompts. Happy today reads Loom cards; it does not embed a live TUI.

Fans dispatches out as flying paper envelopes from god's desk to each worker desk (or to the office door for human escalations), one sprite per routed hive message with act-tinted color and needsHuman flag — Happy has no fan-out visualization at all.

Runs a full two-layer liveness oracle (claim.json Tier A/B + renderer-attested MONOTONIC beat.json) with 9 verdict states surfaced identically on FloorStack tiles AND PulsePanel — Happy's vitals plane is RENDER/QUIET/LOUD honesty-spine but does not yet run a floor-state oracle over remote floors.
Renders REMOTE floors' scenes via feed-cast mode + loopback PTY gateway, so all 5 offices' scenes are visible concurrently with each rendering its own cast — Happy is single-surface.

Boots the god with an autonomous `/remote-control` + INITIAL_GOD_PROMPT orientation, watchdogged by a real ack-hook, holding a bootGate against auto-typers — Happy has no first-boot orchestration of this shape.

Executes CLOSING TIME (mail-based graceful shutdown protocol that gets every worker to commit WIP + append state+next-step to memory.md + ACK before teardown) — Happy has no equivalent WIP-safe close ritual.

Reads and honors circuit-breaker state (constrained/stopped) with PRECEDENCE over hook-derived status, pinning the avatar to 'looping' until a real Stop — Happy's honesty-spine doesn't yet have breaker precedence.

Drains outbox→inbox as a first-class main-process router with single-committer git per drain, hop cap, and act taxonomy (request/inform/propose/query/agree/refuse/done) — Happy's file layer is per-thread cards, not a routed hive of messages.

Idle drain / inbox-wake: an idle agent with new inbox mail gets its TUI typed into with an inbox nudge, per-agent NUDGE_COOLDOWN_MS + content dedup + boot-grace guard so multi-agent collaboration doesn't stall — Happy has no equivalent wake primitive.

Distills the whole building into one pulse.json (60s derived-only) covering floors+blockedOnHuman+shipped+burning+narrative+intentsPending and surfaces it as ONE PulsePanel — Happy's vitals doesn't yet have a cross-floor distiller.

Serves a phone-facing copilot PWA with god-reply bubbles (main/copilot-pwa/) so remote-permission-approval works from anywhere — Happy IS the PWA answer here, but the god-reply-bubble UX is a live artifact worth studying.
Renders TWO parallel shells (classic App + crew CrewShell) with the office scene reusable in both — proves posture-shift can happen without re-writing the sim.

Hosts a `hive/bin/cth-hook.cjs` shim + `hive/bin/merged-ptu.cjs` (lane beat + budget-breaker loop detection) written by the main process on every bootstrap — the mechanism by which real `claude` sessions become hive-aware without touching global settings.

Renders a floor operability layer (click-to-select, hover-tooltip, feet selection ring) directly on the Pixi scene so the metaphor IS the control — Happy today mediates control through separate action rails.

Cost-accounting IS wired: session_id captured from hook payloads, doubles as `--resume` key + AgentUsageSample dedup key, ledger under hive root — Happy tracks tokens but not per-session provider ID lineage.
surprising_findings: The 'boring-when-healthy' / 'banned-gerund' thought-line invariant Carlos mentioned is NOT explicitly enforced anywhere I could find — there's no linter, no policy file, no `bannedWords` array. The COPY happens to lean noun-y ('idle', 'running the floor', 'reading inbox') and gerunds ('compacting context', 'thinking', 'using Read') coexist. The invariant lives in Carlos's/Parthy's authorship discipline, not in code.

There is NO drawn god→worker tree/graph anywhere. The fan-out visualization is 100% flying paper envelopes on the office floor — beautiful, but it means an off-screen or unmounted floor can't visualize a dispatch. Happy shouldn't assume a graph exists to port.

Two entire renderer shells (App.tsx classic + CrewShell.tsx crew) coexist and are picked between at compile time by main.tsx — not a runtime toggle, and NOT dead code. The crew shell has extensive M0..M8 milestone proof scaffolding (CREW_PROOF=false in prod but the sentinels, PROOF_ROOT paths, and instrumentation are all still present) — a lot of the crew code is 'proven, wired for QA in worktree'.

Cockpit-v2's cross-posture density adaptation is NOT in the building — the classic office floor is a fixed full-screen PixiJS scene, and the crew shell is a fixed lazygit 3-pane. Neither is mobile-adaptive. If Happy absorbs the office scene it has to solve the responsive question the building never had to.

Non-Claude providers can be spawned but cannot drain hive inbox — direct hive mail to them is repackaged by `terminalWorkOrderPrompt` and QUEUED as a PTY-typed message via the same idle-only drain used for human-composed messages (see `onHiveTerminalHandoff` in useHive.ts). This is an interesting universal-provider adapter pattern: hive-agnostic mail → per-provider delivery mechanism.

There's a whole embedded IPC surface for `remotePtyBridge` + `ptyGateway` + `remoteTranscript` (main/remotePtyBridge.ts, main/ptyGateway.ts, crew/remoteTranscript.ts) supporting a loopback gateway model where a remote floor's PTYs can be bridged over the local network. Not just 'read the transcript file' — it's a real port+token bridge. Feels more sophisticated than Happy's current session-doc-file model.

The demo/mock event loop (`mockEvents.ts` + `cth:demo-handoff` window event) is CAGED with a very careful gate: opt-in `VITE_CTH_DEMO=1` OR a genuinely empty floor, AND stops the instant the first real PTY agent appears. This is the exact posture-adaptive discipline the honesty spine demands — 'boring when healthy', 'never fake liveness' — but expressed in a demo-loop context. Elegant.

The awareness spine failure-mode is inverted correctly: an error-boundary CATCHES a render throw, the beat stops, main stops writing beat.json, oracle reads WEDGED. So a broken cockpit reads as broken from OUTSIDE the process — a discipline Happy should copy verbatim.

There is an `assistant` role — Michael's prep assistant (Dwight?) that enriches prompts before forwarding them to god (`isAssistant` on AgentMeta, `enrichTaskPrompt`, ASSISTANT_MODEL constant). Send-only: excluded from broadcast fan-out so it never drains an inbox. This is a two-tier agent hierarchy (god + assistant + workers) that neither the spec nor cockpit-v2 currently model.

The CrewShell has 2017 lines and a top-of-file M0..M8.4 sentinel array including facilities/PA/mailroom milestones. Facilities panel, PA broadcast panel, morning report — a whole 'building runs itself' set of surfaces that go beyond what cockpit-v2 has scoped.

cast.ts binds an AGENT to a canonical character face via `castForAgent(agent)` — the SAME function used by the sprite AND by SpritePortrait.tsx, so the tile portrait always matches the walking sprite. Identity coherence discipline explicitly comment-marked (2026-06-12) — worth carrying into Happy as an invariant.

data_hooks.honest_death_status: HONEST-DEAD-CAPABLE. Uses fast-deep-equal/es6 to correctly diff Map payloads. hasContent is set inside the hook file (verified) so an emptied roster still goes LOUD.

data_hooks.name: useVisibleSessionListViewData
data_hooks.feed: reads useSessionListViewData (local sync engine's projection over Socket.io sessions) — not a polled HTTP feed, so no useHonestFeed
data_hooks.honest_death_status: N/A for feed-death honesty (comes from the sync-engine reducer, not an HTTP oracle). TheWorkPlane still treats data===null as 'first paint' (quiet) rather than a fake empty board.

data_hooks.name: useVram
data_hooks.feed: poll GET /v1/vram via useHonestFeed (default 5s cadence, server ts-age staleness backstop)
data_hooks.honest_death_status: PARTIAL. data_hooks.name: useDisk

data_hooks.honest_death_status: PARTIAL — same as useVram: no hasContent predicate, so a stealth-empty view can mask a real outage. Flagged in the Slice 2 desk-verify.

data_hooks.name: useHeartbeat

data_hooks.honest_death_status: PARTIAL — no hasContent predicate. Same flagged gap as useVram/useDisk.

data_hooks.name: useBacklog

Absorbing the assistant tier means extending the seat schema with an explicit parent/role edge, which affects roster, sync-engine, and every downstream consumer. absorb_but_needs_design.item: Hive on-disk routed mail (outbox/inbox drain + act taxonomy request/inform/propose/query/agree/refuse/done)
absorb_but_needs_design.why_needs_design: Happy's file-layer is per-thread cards; the building is per-agent mail with a single-committer git router. Making Happy speak hive mail is a first-class server work-item (new /v1/hive/route endpoint? sync-engine reducer for mail events?) and a schema decision on whether Happy adopts the act enum. Big surface, bright-line-adjacent.

absorb_but_needs_design.item: Two-layer floor-state oracle (claim.json + monotonic beat.json + 9 verdict enum)
absorb_but_needs_design.why_needs_design: AwarenessBeat error-boundary is absorbable now (small); the FULL claim/beat/mutex oracle with 9 verdict states is a rethink of how remote seats prove liveness through Happy's server. Currently useHeartbeat conflates freshness with aliveness (daemonAlive is hard-true). A real port needs a server-side verdict computer and a schema for claim/beat that a remote daemon writes. Big enough to be its own slice.

The building's remotePtyBridge + ptyGateway is a real port+token bridge for cross-floor terminal streaming. Happy's equivalent needs to decide whether streams flow through the encrypted sync channel (e2e-preserving) or a separate transport, and how key material is handled on Tauri vs phone. Ties directly to the live-tail slice above but is a bigger transport question.

do_not_absorb.item: Full PixiJS OfficeFloor walking-avatar scene as the primary surface
do_not_absorb.reason: 1895 lines, PixiJS v8 with unsafe-eval CSP shim, Tiled map + tilesets, A* pathfinding — desktop-only tech that shatters the multi-surface invariant Happy is built on. Absorbing it as-is would fork the codebase back into a desktop-primary posture and undo Slice 3. See PIXI VERDICT below for the split.

do_not_absorb.item: Dual-shell architecture (App.tsx + CrewShell.tsx picked at build time)
do_not_absorb.reason: The building has TWO renderer shells because it grew that way; Happy's whole point post-Slice-3 is ONE component tree at three densities. Adopting a build-time shell switch is a regression.

do_not_absorb.item: Electron-specific main-process primitives (Tier B named-mutex holder child PowerShell, node-pty, WebGL xterm as PRIMARY surface)
do_not_absorb.reason: Named kernel mutexes and PowerShell child processes are Windows/Electron-only; node-pty doesn't exist in a phone runtime. These stay as building-side implementation details; Happy consumes their outputs via server APIs but never runs them locally.

Happy already has a stronger discipline via useHonestFeed's three-state RENDER/QUIET/LOUD and the QUIET-when-empty-and-healthy invariant; a demo loop would tempt fake-liveness violations. If a demo mode is needed for onboarding it should be built on the honesty spine, not ported.

do_not_absorb.item: Full CrewShell M0..M8 milestone-proof scaffolding (facilities panel, PA broadcast panel, morning report, 2017-line shell)
do_not_absorb.reason: That's 'building runs itself' surface area that is out of scope for the work-first cockpit and would drag Happy into building-scope. Absorb specific atoms (PulsePanel, NeedsYouStrip, FloorStack) not the shell.
Happy IS the phone-cockpit answer here. The god-reply-bubble UX is worth studying for the LiveOutputTail phone fallback but the embedded PWA itself is superseded by Happy.

do_not_absorb.item: cth-hook.cjs shim + merged-ptu.cjs written into every session on bootstrap
do_not_absorb.reason: Deep coupling to the building's hive-hook wire format. Happy should receive hive events through its own server API rather than reproduce the hook-shim bootstrap discipline in a mobile app.

delta.the_pixi_scene_verdict: DEFER-AND-ABSTRACT (split verdict). Do NOT absorb the PixiJS OfficeFloor as a primary surface in Slice 4 or 5 — it is desktop-only and would break the multi-surface capability-invariance Slice 3 just proved. But the METAPHOR is load-bearing ("the fan-out is visible / fun to watch") and cannot be discarded either. Split: (1) IMMEDIATE — abstract the metaphor into three cross-surface primitives that DO travel: an existing WorkerFanout strip (shipped), a lightweight per-lane 'inbound envelope' pulse ring on the avatar (new, cheap, works on RN+Web), and a dispatch-ledger row in the expanded LaneTile detail. Together these give you 'the fan-out is visible' without a scene. (2) LATER (Slice 6+, after cutover) — reintroduce the full walking scene as a Tauri-desktop-ONLY 'office view' route (a lens onto the same congress-roster + hive-message feed, feed-cast pattern from the building). Phone/deck never see it; desktop optionally opens it as a second surface. This preserves the fun-to-watch heart on the device where it belongs, without regressing the primary cockpit. Rationale: the walking scene's operability layer (11 onAgentSelect/onAgentHover call sites confirmed) proves the click-to-select model works, but that model is duplicative of tapping a LaneTile — it is delight, not capability. Delight belongs behind the capability, not in front of it.
ranked_next_moves: 1. BUILD LiveOutputTail (persistent xterm on web/Tauri, plain scroll on phone) backed by a new useLaneTail hook that streams assistant messages from the sync engine — this is the largest visible §2 gap and unlocks the 'spawn one to see real Claude output' promise. Desk-designs, sonnet-builds the port.
2. DECIDE the push gate for lane/happy-dev (78 commits deep, no remote branch, deploys on push). This is Slice 4's terminal blocker per spec §7 — must precede cutover. Carlos-only call.

3. BUILD the Slice-2 hygiene backfill batch: hasContent on useVram/useDisk/useHeartbeat + AbortController threading through useHonestFeed + VitalsStrip posture threading. All three are small sonnet-lane items that close acknowledged flags before cockpit-v2 becomes the live daily driver.

4. BUILD AwarenessBeat + monotonic-beat honesty spine — a react error-boundary at cockpit-v2 root that stops a beat on render-death so a wedged cockpit reads WEDGED from outside the process. Cheap, high-value, and required-in-spirit before cutover.

5. BUILD consequential-confirm knock-card variants (COST / GIT-push / DESTRUCTIVE) — bright-lines must travel with the surface before the surface becomes the daily driver. Desk-designs the UX (cannot swipe-dismiss, capability-invariant across densities), sonnet-builds.
open_forks_for_carlos: Push gate for lane/happy-dev: cutover to live cannot happen until you green-light pushing 78 local commits (Vesta/desktop deploys on push per spec §7). This is the Slice 4 terminal blocker — the desk cannot make this call alone.

PixiJS scene posture: DEFER-AND-ABSTRACT is the desk's recommendation, but the alternatives (a) absorb full scene as Tauri-only primary; (b) build a low-fi cross-surface scene from day one; (c) drop the scene entirely as delight-not-capability — are all live. This is a taste call about how much of the building's soul travels.

Live-output-tail transport: does the streaming Claude-byte tail flow through the encrypted sync channel (preserves e2e, more work) or a separate server-mediated PTY-bridge transport (faster to ship, weaker crypto story)? Bright-line-adjacent because it touches how 'files are self' extends to a byte stream.

Two-tier assistant/god hierarchy: absorbing the building's assistant role (Dwight enriches prompts before god) requires extending CongressSeatSchema with a parent/role edge, which ripples into every roster consumer. Ship it as a schema change, or leave as building-only and let Happy render only the flat god+workers view?

Where the cockpit-v2 route lives at cutover: replace SessionsList.tsx default export vs land CockpitV2 as (app)/_layout.tsx default landing surface. Also: what happens to SessionsList's browse-chrome (date/project headers, archive toggle) — absorbed into a secondary view, or dropped per spec §2's 'every lane as an equal tile' implication?
